_comment: U12, multi-user authentication and per-user ownership.
Access control is the worst possible fit for a passing test suite as evidence, because
every one of these mutations leaves a working application. Log in, see your clips, render
one, download it - all fine. The only difference is that somebody else can see them too,
and nothing in the product ever says so. There is no exception, no log line and no
degraded output; the failure is invisible from the inside, which is exactly the shape the
Groups: the authorization rule itself, the middleware choke point (including the /clips
mount, which route dependencies would not have covered), session lifetime and revocation,
password storage, the login brute-force and enumeration guards, and the ownership stamp
that has to survive a restart.

mutations.name: everyone_may_access_every_job
mutations.why: the whole authorization rule removed; the app works perfectly and every user sees every other user's clips

mutations.name: unowned_jobs_are_public
mutations.why: every job that predates U12 has no owner, so treating unowned as public hands the existing library to the first account created after enabling auth

mutations.name: a_missing_job_is_accessible
mutations.old:
if job is None:
        return False
mutations.new:
if job is None:
        return True
mutations.why: an id that resolves to nothing must answer like an id that is not yours, or the difference makes job ids enumerable

mutations.name: admin_check_dropped
mutations.old:
if not user.is_admin:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="This action requires an administrator.")
mutations.why: any signed-in user could then create accounts and disable others - privilege escalation with no error anywhere

mutations.name: middleware_lets_anonymous_through
mutations.why: authentication becomes decoration: the UI still shows a login form and the API answers everyone

mutations.name: everything_is_exempt
mutations.why: the exempt list is the one place a mistake opens every endpoint at once

mutations.name: clips_mount_ungated
mutations.old: if path.startswith(CLIPS_PREFIX) and not self._may_read_media(path, user):
mutations.why: the media IS the product, and StaticFiles is a mount rather than a route - this is precisely what route dependencies would have missed while every JSON endpoint looked protected

mutations.name: media_without_a_job_record_is_served
mutations.why: clips outlive their records - the job table is pruned to MAX_PERSISTED_JOBS while the files stay - so failing open leaks precisely the longest-standing users' clips

mutations.name: authorised_job_skips_the_check
mutations.old: if job is None or not may_access_job(job, current_user(request)):
mutations.why: the single funnel every job-scoped endpoint goes through; without the second clause each one authenticates and none authorises

mutations.name: job_list_is_not_filtered
mutations.why: every user's dashboard would list every job in the instance, titles and all, before any per-job check is reached

mutations.name: new_jobs_are_unowned
mutations.old:
user = current_user(request)
    return user.id if user is not None else ""
mutations.why: jobs created with auth on would belong to nobody, so a user could not see the work they just submitted while every admin could

mutations.name: logout_leaves_the_session_alive
mutations.why: the cookie is cleared so the UI looks signed out, while a captured token keeps working for a fortnight

mutations.name: password_change_skips_the_current_password
mutations.old:
if store.authenticate(user.username, req.current_password or "") is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Current password is incorrect.")
mutations.why: a borrowed session becomes a permanent account takeover

mutations.name: password_change_keeps_other_sessions
mutations.why: changing a password is what you do when you think a session is stolen; leaving the others alive defeats the only reason to do it

mutations.name: cookie_is_readable_by_javascript
mutations.why: one XSS bug anywhere in the SPA then yields session tokens; this flag is the reason the token is not in localStorage either

mutations.name: cookie_sent_cross_site
mutations.why: SameSite=Lax is the CSRF defence here; without it any site can make state-changing requests with the user's cookie

mutations.name: session_expiry_not_enforced_on_read
mutations.why: sessions would live until something swept, so shortening the TTL - or an expiry passing - would have no effect on anyone already signed in

mutations.name: disabled_users_keep_their_sessions
mutations.old: if user_row is None or bool(user_row["disabled"]):
mutations.why: the account check has to be against current state; otherwise disabling somebody does nothing until their cookie expires

mutations.name: disabling_does_not_revoke
mutations.old:
if disabled:
                conn.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?", (user_id,))
mutations.why: same failure from the other side: the row says disabled and the live session says otherwise

mutations.name: session_tokens_stored_in_plaintext
mutations.why: a copy of users.db would then be a set of live sessions, which is the same class of mistake as storing plaintext passwords

mutations.name: disabled_accounts_can_authenticate
mutations.why: a disabled account could sign in again and get a fresh session, making the whole control cosmetic

mutations.name: usernames_become_case_sensitive
mutations.why: 'Alice' and 'alice' as separate accounts is a phishing surface inside your own tool, and every user who capitalises their name appears to have no account

mutations.name: password_salt_is_constant
mutations.why: identical passwords become identical rows, so one cracked hash cracks every account that shares it and a rainbow table becomes worthwhile

mutations.name: password_floor_removed
mutations.why: length is the property that actually matters, and this is the only place it is enforced

mutations.name: rehash_never_needed
mutations.old: return (have_n, have_r, have_p, len(key)) != (n, r, p, KEY_BYTES)
mutations.why: raising the cost would then apply only to new accounts, and a successful login is the only moment an old hash can be upgraded

mutations.name: corrupt_hash_reported_as_current
mutations.why: an unreadable hash can never be verified against, so it must be replaced at the next opportunity rather than kept for ever

mutations.name: verify_uses_plain_equality
mutations.why: declared equivalent: `==` and compare_digest agree on every input, so no functional test can tell them apart - the difference is wall-clock timing on a mismatch, which this suite deliberately does not assert on because a timing test on a shared CI runner measures the runner. Included to record *why* the code uses compare_digest, and to be explicit that the guarantee is unproven by tests rather than quietly assumed to be covered.

mutations.name: rate_limit_never_triggers
mutations.why: an offline-speed password guessing loop against a live endpoint, with nothing in the logs that looks different from normal use

mutations.name: rate_limit_forgets_failures
mutations.why: the same hole from the other side: the check runs and the counter never rises

mutations.name: rate_limit_window_ignored
mutations.old:
cutoff = time.time() - self._window()
        key = (username, client)
        with self._lock:
            recent = [t for t in self._attempts.get(key, []) if t > cutoff]
            self._attempts[key] = recent
            return len(recent) < limit
mutations.new:
key = (username, client)
        with self._lock:
            recent = list(self._attempts.get(key, []))
            return len(recent) < limit
mutations.why: without the window a user who once mistyped their password accumulates towards a permanent lockout

mutations.name: bootstrap_starts_with_no_way_in
mutations.old:
if not username or not password:
        raise RuntimeError(
mutations.why: auth enabled with an empty user table means every login fails; a server that boots and can only answer 401 is far harder to diagnose than one that refuses to boot and says why

mutations.name: bootstrap_admin_is_not_an_admin
mutations.why: the first account could not then create the second, and there would be no way to administer the instance at all

mutations.name: owner_dropped_from_the_persisted_record
mutations.why: ownership would hold until the process restarted and then every job would read back unowned - visible to admins, invisible to the person who made it

mutations.name: owner_not_restored_from_the_record
mutations.why: the same loss on the read side, which is the half a to_dict test alone would not notice

mutations.name: job_store_ignores_the_owner_filter
mutations.new: return sorted(jobs, key=lambda j: j.created_at, reverse=True)
mutations.why: the filter the API relies on for every listing; without it the per-request owner argument is accepted and discarded

mutations.name: submit_discards_the_owner
mutations.why: the one line that attaches a new job to the person who asked for it
